title.zh: 卷9 列傳第1 皇后
title.raw: 卷9 列傳第1 皇后 Volume 9 Biographies 1: Empresses

sentences.zh: 文帝元皇后 文宣叱奴皇后 孝閔帝元皇后 明帝獨孤皇后 武帝阿史那皇后 武帝李皇后 宣帝楊皇后 宣帝朱皇后 宣帝陳皇后 宣帝元皇后 宣帝尉遲皇后 靜帝司馬皇后

translations.literal: Empress Yuan, consort of Emperor Wen  Empress Chinu, consort of Emperor Wen  Empress Yuan, consort of Emperor Min  Empress Dugu, consort of Emperor Ming  Empress Ashina, consort of Emperor Wu  Empress Li, consort of Emperor Wu  Empress Yang, consort of Emperor Xuan  Empress Zhu, consort of Emperor Xuan  Empress Chen, consort of Emperor Xuan  Empress Yuan, consort of Emperor Xuan  Empress Yuchi, consort of Emperor Xuan  Empress Sima, consort of Emperor Jing
translations.idiomatic: Empress Yuan, consort of Emperor Wen Yuwen Tai; Empress Chinu, consort of Emperor Wen Yuwen Tai; Empress Yuan, consort of Emperor Min Yuwen Jue; Empress Dugu, consort of Emperor Ming Yuwen Yu; Empress Ashina, consort of Emperor Wu Yuwen Yong; Empress Li, consort of Emperor Wu Yuwen Yong; Empress Yang, consort of Emperor Xuan Yuwen Yun; Empress Zhu, consort of Emperor Xuan Yuwen Yun; Empress Chen, consort of Emperor Xuan Yuwen Yun; Empress Yuan, consort of Emperor Xuan Yuwen Yun; Empress Yuchi, consort of Emperor Xuan Yuwen Yun; Empress Sima, consort of Emperor Jing Yuwen Chan

sentences.zh: 《書》紀有虞之德，載「厘降二女」；

translations.literal: The Book of Documents records the virtue of Yu Shun, stating "He descended and gave his two daughters [in marriage]";
translations.idiomatic: The Book of Documents records the virtue of Yu Shun, stating "He descended and gave his two daughters [in marriage]";

sentences.zh: 《詩》述文王之美，稱「刑于寡妻」。

translations.literal: The Book of Poetry describes the beauty of King Wen, praising "He took his example from his wife alone."
translations.idiomatic: The Book of Poetry describes the beauty of King Wen, praising "He took his example from his wife alone."

sentences.zh: 是知婚姻之道，男女之別，實有國有家者之所慎也。

translations.literal: Thus one knows that the way of marriage and the distinction between men and women are matters those who have a state and a family must carefully observe.
translations.idiomatic: Thus one knows that the way of marriage and the distinction between men and women are matters that rulers of states and households must carefully observe.

sentences.zh: 自三代迄于魏晉，興衰之數，得失之迹，備乎傳記，故其詳可得聞焉。

translations.literal: From the Three Dynasties down to Wei and Jin, the pattern of rise and fall and the traces of gain and loss are fully set forth in the records, so the details may be heard.
translations.idiomatic: From the Three Dynasties down to Wei and Jin, the cycles of rise and fall and the traces of success and failure are fully recorded, so the details may be known.

sentences.zh: 若娉納以德，防閑以禮，大義正於宮闈，王化行於邦國，則坤儀式固，而鼎命惟永矣。

translations.literal: If one selects consorts by virtue and guards against impropriety by ritual, if great principle is upheld within the palace and royal transformation is carried out in the realm, then the feminine standard is firmly established and the dynastic mandate endures forever.
translations.idiomatic: If consorts are chosen by virtue and the inner quarters are guarded by ritual, if great principle holds within the palace and royal teaching spreads through the realm, then the queenly model stands firm and the dynastic mandate endures.

sentences.zh: 至於邪僻旣進，法度莫修，冶容迷其主心，私謁蠹其朝政，則風化淩替，而宗社不守矣。

translations.literal: When the perverse and depraved gain entry and laws and standards are not maintained, when alluring appearance bewilders the lord's heart and private audiences corrupt court governance, then custom and teaching collapse and the ancestral altars are not preserved.
translations.idiomatic: When the wicked gain access and law and order fall into neglect, when seductive beauty confuses the ruler's mind and private audiences corrupt government, then custom collapses and the altars of state are lost.

sentences.zh: 夫然者，豈非皇王之龜鑑與。

translations.literal: Is this not a mirror for emperors and kings?
translations.idiomatic: Is this not a mirror held up for emperors and kings?

sentences.zh: 周氏率由姬制，內職有序。

translations.literal: The Zhou house followed the Ji system, and the inner offices were orderly.
translations.idiomatic: The Zhou house followed the Zhou institutional model, and the inner palaces were well ordered.

sentences.zh: 太祖創基，修衽席以儉約；

translations.literal: The Grand Progenitor Yuwen Tai founded the base and maintained the marital bedchamber in frugality;
translations.idiomatic: Grand Progenitor Yuwen Tai laid the foundation and kept the inner quarters in frugal simplicity;

sentences.zh: 高祖嗣曆，節情欲於矯枉。

translations.literal: High Ancestor Yuwen Yong succeeded to the throne and restrained passions in correcting excess.
translations.idiomatic: High Ancestor Yuwen Yong succeeded to the throne and checked excess by restraining his passions.

sentences.zh: 宮闈有貫魚之美，戚里無私溺之尤，可謂得人君體也。

translations.literal: The inner palaces had the beauty of "the lined fish," and the imperial kindred had no extreme indulgence in favoritism—this may be called grasping the ruler's proper style.
translations.idiomatic: The inner palaces showed the ordered beauty of "the lined fish," and the imperial kindred knew no gross favoritism—this may be called understanding the ruler's proper bearing.

sentences.zh: 宣皇外行其志，內逞其欲，溪壑難滿，采擇無厭。

translations.literal: Emperor Xuan Yuwen Yun outwardly pursued his ambitions while inwardly indulging his desires; gullies and ravines could not be filled, and selection never ceased.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xuan Yuwen Yun outwardly pursued his ambitions while inwardly indulging his desires; his appetite was insatiable, and his taking of consorts never ceased.

sentences.zh: 恩之所加，莫限廝皂；

translations.literal: Those whom favor reached were not limited to menials;
translations.idiomatic: Those whom his favor reached were not limited to the lowest servants;

sentences.zh: 榮之所及，無隔險詖。

translations.literal: Those whom glory touched knew no barrier of remoteness or partiality.
translations.idiomatic: Those whom glory touched knew no barrier of distance or partiality.

sentences.zh: 於是升蘭殿而正位，踐椒庭而齊體者，非一人焉；

translations.literal: Thus those who ascended the Orchid Hall to take proper rank and tread the pepper courtyard as full equals were not one person alone;
translations.idiomatic: Thus those who ascended the Orchid Hall to take formal rank and shared the pepper courtyard as full equals were not one person alone;

sentences.zh: 階房帷而拖青紫，承恩幸而擁玉帛者，非一族焉。

translations.literal: Those who in side chambers donned purple and crimson and, receiving favor, clutched jade and silk were not one clan alone.
translations.idiomatic: Those who in side chambers donned purple and crimson and, receiving favor, grasped jade and silk were not one clan alone.

sentences.zh: 雖辛、癸之荒淫，趙、李之傾惑，曾未足比其髣髴也。

translations.literal: Even the debauchery of Xin and Gui and the deluding influence of Zhao and Li barely approach this in likeness.
translations.idiomatic: Even the debauchery of Kings Zhou and Li of old and the seductive sway of Zhao Feiyan and Lady Li of Han barely approach this in likeness.

sentences.zh: 民厭苛政，弊事實多，太祖之祚忽諸，特由於此。

translations.literal: The people grew weary of harsh government, and abuses were truly many; the mandate of the Grand Progenitor ended in a flash, chiefly because of this.
translations.idiomatic: The people grew weary of harsh government, and abuses were many; the Zhou mandate established by Grand Progenitor Yuwen Tai ended in a flash, largely for this reason.

sentences.zh: 故敘其事以為《皇后傳》云。

translations.literal: Therefore I narrate these affairs as the Biographies of Empresses.
translations.idiomatic: Therefore I narrate these affairs as the Biographies of Empresses.

sentences.zh: 文帝元皇后，魏孝武帝之妹。

translations.literal: Empress Yuan, consort of Emperor Wen Yuwen Tai, was a younger sister of Emperor Xiaowu of Wei.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Yuan, consort of Emperor Wen Yuwen Tai, was a younger sister of Emperor Xiaowu of Wei.

sentences.zh: 初封平原公主，適開府張歡。

translations.literal: Initially enfeoffed as Princess of Pingyuan, she was given in marriage to Zhang Huan, opening-the-feudatory.
translations.idiomatic: Initially enfeoffed as Princess of Pingyuan, she was given in marriage to Zhang Huan, opening-the-feudatory.

sentences.zh: 歡性貪殘，遇后無禮，又嘗殺后侍婢。

translations.literal: Huan was greedy and cruel; he treated the empress without courtesy, and once even killed her serving maid.
translations.idiomatic: Huan was greedy and cruel; he treated the empress without courtesy, and once even killed one of her serving maids.

sentences.zh: 后怒，訴之於帝，帝乃執歡殺之。

translations.literal: The empress in anger complained to the emperor, and the emperor had Huan seized and executed.
translations.idiomatic: The empress in anger appealed to the emperor, and the emperor had Huan seized and executed.

sentences.zh: 改封后為馮翊公主，以配太祖，生孝閔帝。

translations.literal: The empress was re-enfeoffed as Princess of Fengyi and given as wife to the Grand Progenitor; she bore Emperor Min Yuwen Jue.
translations.idiomatic: The empress was re-enfeoffed as Princess of Fengyi and given in marriage to Grand Progenitor Yuwen Tai; she bore Emperor Min Yuwen Jue.

sentences.zh: 大統七年，薨。

translations.literal: In the seventh year of Datong she died.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year of Datong she died.

sentences.zh: 魏恭帝三年十二月，合葬成陵。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month of the third year of Emperor Gong of Wei, she was buried with him at Chengling.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month of the third year of Emperor Gong of Wei, she was buried with him at Chengling.

sentences.zh: 孝閔帝踐祚，追尊為王后。

translations.literal: When Emperor Min Yuwen Jue ascended the throne, she was posthumously honored as queen.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Min Yuwen Jue ascended the throne, she was posthumously honored as queen.

sentences.zh: 武成初，又追尊為皇后。

translations.literal: In the beginning of Wucheng, she was again posthumously honored as empress.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Wucheng, she was again posthumously honored as empress.

sentences.zh: 文宣叱奴皇后，代人也。

translations.literal: Empress Chinu, consort of Emperor Wen Yuwen Tai, was a native of Dai.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Chinu, consort of Emperor Wen Yuwen Tai, was a native of Dai.

sentences.zh: 太祖為丞相，納后為姬，生高祖。

translations.literal: When the Grand Progenitor Yuwen Tai was chief minister, he took her as consort; she bore High Ancestor Yuwen Yong.
translations.idiomatic: When Grand Progenitor Yuwen Tai was chief minister, he took her as consort; she bore High Ancestor Yuwen Yong.

sentences.zh: 天和

translations.literal: Tianhe
translations.idiomatic: Tianhe

translations.literal: (first)
translations.idiomatic: (first)

sentences.zh: 年六月，尊為皇太后。

translations.literal: year, sixth month, she was honored as empress dowager.
translations.idiomatic: year, sixth month, she was honored as empress dowager.

sentences.zh: 建德

translations.literal: Jiande
translations.idiomatic: Jiande

translations.literal: (second)
translations.idiomatic: (second)

sentences.zh: 年三月癸酉，崩。

translations.literal: year, third month, on guiyou day, she died.
translations.idiomatic: year, third month, on guiyou day, she died.

sentences.zh: 四月丁巳，葬〔永〕固陵。

translations.literal: Fourth month, on dingsi day, she was buried at [Yong] Guling.
translations.idiomatic: Fourth month, on dingsi day, she was buried at [Yong] Guling.

sentences.zh: 明帝獨孤皇后，太保、衛國公信之長女。

translations.literal: Empress Dugu, consort of Emperor Ming Yuwen Yu, was the eldest daughter of Grand Guardian and Duke of Weiguo Xin.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Dugu, consort of Emperor Ming Yuwen Yu, was the eldest daughter of Grand Guardian and Duke of Weiguo Dugu Xin.

sentences.zh: 帝之在藩也，納為夫人。

translations.literal: While the emperor was still in his princely domain, she was taken as lady.
translations.idiomatic: While Emperor Ming Yuwen Yu was still in his princely domain, she was taken as lady.

sentences.zh: 二年正月，立為王后。

translations.literal: Second year, first month, she was installed as queen.
translations.idiomatic: Second year, first month, she was installed as queen.

sentences.zh: 四月，崩，葬昭陵。

translations.literal: Fourth month, she died and was buried at Zhaoling.
translations.idiomatic: Fourth month, she died and was buried at Zhaoling.

sentences.zh: 武成初，追崇為皇后。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Wucheng, she was posthumously honored as empress.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Wucheng, she was posthumously honored as empress.

sentences.zh: 世宗崩，與后合葬。

translations.literal: When Emperor Ming Yuwen Yu died, she was buried with him.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Ming Yuwen Yu died, she was buried with him.

sentences.zh: 武帝阿史那皇后，突厥木扞可汗俟斤之女。

translations.literal: Empress Ashina, consort of Emperor Wu Yuwen Yong, was the daughter of Irkin, khan of the Turks, Muhan Khan.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Ashina, consort of Emperor Wu Yuwen Yong, was the daughter of Irkin, khan of the Turks, Muhan Khan.

sentences.zh: 突厥滅茹茹之後，盡有塞表之地，控弦數十萬，志陵中夏。

translations.literal: After the Turks destroyed the Rouran, they held all the lands beyond the frontier and commanded several hundred thousand bowmen, their ambition set on dominating China.
translations.idiomatic: After the Turks destroyed the Rouran, they held all the lands beyond the frontier and commanded several hundred thousand bowmen, with their ambition set on dominating China.

sentences.zh: 太祖方與齊人爭衡，結以為援。

translations.literal: The Grand Progenitor Yuwen Tai was then contending with the Qi for supremacy and sought alliance with them.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Progenitor Yuwen Tai was then contending with Northern Qi for supremacy and sought alliance with the Turks.

sentences.zh: 俟斤初欲以女配帝，旣而悔之。

translations.literal: Irkin at first wished to give his daughter to the emperor, but afterward regretted it.
translations.idiomatic: Irkin at first wished to give his daughter to the Zhou emperor, but afterward changed his mind.

sentences.zh: 高祖卽位，前後累遣使要結，乃許歸后於我。

translations.literal: When High Ancestor Yuwen Yong ascended the throne, envoys were repeatedly sent to renew the alliance, and he finally agreed to send the empress to us.
translations.idiomatic: When High Ancestor Yuwen Yong ascended the throne, envoys were repeatedly sent to renew the alliance, and Irkin finally agreed to send the empress to Zhou.

sentences.zh: 保定五年二月，詔陳國公純、許國公宇文貴、神武公竇毅、南

translations.literal: Second month of the fifth year of Baoding, an edict ordered Duke of Chen Yuwen Chun, Duke of Xu Yuwen Gui, Duke of Shenwu Dou Yi, and Nan
translations.idiomatic: Second month of the fifth year of Baoding, an edict ordered Duke of Chen Yuwen Chun, Duke of Xu Yuwen Gui, Duke of Shenwu Dou Yi, and Nan

translations.literal: (Yang)
translations.idiomatic: (Yang)

sentences.zh: 〔安〕公楊薦等，奉備皇后文物及行殿，幷六宮以下百二十人，至俟斤牙帳所，迎后。

translations.literal: [An] Duke Yang Jian and others, bearing the empress's regalia and traveling hall, together with one hundred twenty persons of the six palaces and below, went to Irkin's encampment to welcome the empress.
translations.idiomatic: [An] Duke Yang Jian and others, bearing the empress's regalia and traveling hall, together with one hundred twenty persons of the six palaces and below, went to Irkin's encampment to welcome the empress.

sentences.zh: 俟斤又許齊人以婚，將有異志。

translations.literal: Irkin again promised his daughter in marriage to the Qi, and was about to change his allegiance.
translations.idiomatic: Irkin again promised his daughter in marriage to Northern Qi, and was about to shift his allegiance.

sentences.zh: 純等在彼累載，不得反命。

translations.literal: Chun and the others remained there for years and could not return with their mission accomplished.
translations.idiomatic: Yuwen Chun and the others remained there for years and could not return with their mission accomplished.

sentences.zh: 雖諭之以信義，俟斤不從。

translations.literal: Although they admonished him with faith and righteousness, Irkin would not comply.
translations.idiomatic: Although they admonished him with faith and righteousness, Irkin would not comply.

sentences.zh: 會大雷風起，飄壞其穹廬等，旬日不止。

translations.literal: Then great thunder and wind arose, blowing down their felt tents and the like, and did not cease for ten days.
translations.idiomatic: Then great thunder and wind arose, blowing down their felt tents and the like, and did not cease for ten days.

sentences.zh: 俟斤大懼，以為天譴，乃備禮送后。

translations.literal: Irkin was greatly frightened, taking it for heavenly punishment, and thereupon prepared full rites to send the empress off.
translations.idiomatic: Irkin was greatly frightened, taking it for heavenly punishment, and thereupon prepared full rites to send the empress off.

translations.literal: (And)
translations.idiomatic: (And)

sentences.zh: 純等設行殿，列羽儀，奉之以歸。

translations.literal: Chun and the others set up the traveling hall, arrayed the guard of honor, and escorted her back.
translations.idiomatic: Yuwen Chun and the others set up the traveling hall, arrayed the guard of honor, and escorted her back.

sentences.zh: 天和三年三月，后至，高祖行親迎之禮。

translations.literal: Third month of the third year of Tianhe, the empress arrived; High Ancestor Yuwen Yong performed the rite of greeting her in person.
translations.idiomatic: Third month of the third year of Tianhe, the empress arrived; High Ancestor Yuwen Yong performed the rite of greeting her in person.

sentences.zh: 后有姿貌，善容止，高祖深敬焉。

translations.literal: The empress had fine appearance and graceful bearing; High Ancestor Yuwen Yong deeply respected her.
translations.idiomatic: The empress had fine appearance and graceful bearing; High Ancestor Yuwen Yong deeply respected her.

sentences.zh: 宣帝卽位，尊為皇太后。

translations.literal: When Emperor Xuan Yuwen Yun ascended the throne, she was honored as empress dowager.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Xuan Yuwen Yun ascended the throne, she was honored as empress dowager.

sentences.zh: 大象元年二月，改為天元皇太后。

translations.literal: Second month of the first year of Daxiang, she was retitled Heavenly Primordial Empress Dowager.
translations.idiomatic: Second month of the first year of Daxiang, she was retitled Heavenly Primordial Empress Dowager.

sentences.zh: 二年二月，又尊為天元上皇太后。

translations.literal: Second month of the second year, she was again honored as Heavenly Primordial Upper Empress Dowager.
translations.idiomatic: Second month of the second year, she was again honored as Heavenly Primordial Upper Empress Dowager.

sentences.zh: 册曰：「天元皇帝臣贇，奉璽綬册，謹上天元皇太后尊號曰天元上皇太后。

translations.literal: The edict of investiture stated: "The Heavenly Primordial Emperor, your subject Yun, reverently presents the seal and cord of investiture and respectfully bestows upon the Heavenly Primordial Empress Dowager the honorific title Heavenly Primordial Upper Empress Dowager.
translations.idiomatic: The edict of investiture stated: "The Heavenly Primordial Emperor, your subject Yun, reverently presents the seal and cord of investiture and respectfully bestows upon the Heavenly Primordial Empress Dowager the honorific title Heavenly Primordial Upper Empress Dowager.

sentences.zh: 伏惟窮神盡智，含弘載物，道洽萬邦，儀刑四海。

translations.literal: I consider that you exhaust the divine and exhaust wisdom, embrace and carry all things, your Way harmonizing with ten thousand states, your model governing the four seas.
translations.idiomatic: I consider that you exhaust the divine and exhaust wisdom, embrace and carry all things, your Way harmonizing with ten thousand states, your model governing the four seas.

sentences.zh: 聖慈訓誘，恩深明德，雖册徽號，未極尊嚴。

translations.literal: Your sage compassion instructs and guides; your grace is deep and your virtue bright—though an honorific title is conferred, it does not reach the full measure of your dignity.
translations.idiomatic: Your sage compassion instructs and guides; your grace is deep and your virtue bright—though an honorific title is conferred, it does not reach the full measure of your dignity.

sentences.zh: 是用增奉鴻名，光縟常禮。

translations.literal: Therefore I add this great name and extend the constant rites.
translations.idiomatic: Therefore I add this great name and extend the constant rites.

sentences.zh: 俾誠敬有展，歡慰在茲，福祉無疆，億兆斯賴。

translations.literal: May sincerity and reverence be fully displayed, joy and comfort rest here, blessings without limit, and the hundred millions rely upon you.
translations.idiomatic: May sincerity and reverence be fully displayed, joy and comfort rest here, blessings without limit, and the hundred millions rely upon you.

sentences.zh: 」宣帝崩，靜帝尊為太皇太后。

translations.literal: " When Emperor Xuan Yuwen Yun died, Emperor Jing Yuwen Chan honored her as grand empress dowager.
translations.idiomatic: " When Emperor Xuan Yuwen Yun died, Emperor Jing Yuwen Chan honored her as grand empress dowager.

sentences.zh: 隋開皇二年殂，年三十二。

translations.literal: In the second year of Kaihuang of Sui she died, aged thirty-two.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Kaihuang of Sui she died, aged thirty-two.

sentences.zh: 隋文帝詔有司備禮册，祔葬於孝陵。

translations.literal: Sui Emperor Wen Yang Jian ordered the officials to prepare rites of investiture and had her buried at Xiaoling.
translations.idiomatic: Sui Emperor Wen Yang Jian ordered the officials to prepare rites of investiture and had her buried at Xiaoling.

sentences.zh: 宣帝楊皇后名麗華，隋文帝長女。

translations.literal: Empress Yang, consort of Emperor Xuan Yuwen Yun, named Lihua, was the eldest daughter of Sui Emperor Wen Yang Jian.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Yang, consort of Emperor Xuan Yuwen Yun, named Lihua, was the eldest daughter of Sui Emperor Wen Yang Jian.

sentences.zh: 帝在東宮，高祖為帝納后為皇太子妃。

translations.literal: While the emperor was in the Eastern Palace, High Ancestor Yuwen Yong had the empress taken as crown prince consort for him.
translations.idiomatic: While Emperor Xuan Yuwen Yun was in the Eastern Palace, High Ancestor Yuwen Yong had her taken as crown prince consort for him.

sentences.zh: 宣政元年閏六月，立為皇后。

translations.literal: Intercalary sixth month of the first year of Xuanzheng, she was installed as empress.
translations.idiomatic: Intercalary sixth month of the first year of Xuanzheng, she was installed as empress.

sentences.zh: 帝后自稱天元皇帝，號后為天元皇后。

translations.literal: The emperor and empress styled themselves Heavenly Primordial Emperor and Heavenly Primordial Empress.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xuan Yuwen Yun and the empress styled themselves Heavenly Primordial Emperor and Heavenly Primordial Empress.

sentences.zh: 尋又立天皇后及左右皇后，與后為四皇后焉。

translations.literal: Soon afterward Heavenly Empress and the Left and Right Empresses were also installed, making four empresses together with her.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward Heavenly Empress and the Left and Right Empresses were also installed, making four empresses together with her.

sentences.zh: 二年，詔曰：「帝降二女，后德所以儷君；

translations.literal: Second year, an edict stated: "The emperor descended his two daughters; the empress's virtue therefore matches the ruler;
translations.idiomatic: Second year, an edict stated: "The emperor descended his two daughters; the empress's virtue therefore matches the ruler;

sentences.zh: 天列四星，妃象於焉垂耀。

translations.literal: Heaven arrayed four stars; the consort's image there sheds its radiance.
translations.idiomatic: Heaven arrayed four stars; the consort's image there sheds its radiance.

sentences.zh: 朕取法上玄，稽諸令典，爰命四后，內正六宮，庶弘贊柔德，廣修粢盛。

translations.literal: We take the Way of High Heaven as model and examine the present statutes; we therefore appoint four empresses to govern the six palaces within, that they may broadly assist in gentle virtue and widely maintain the sacrificial grain."
translations.idiomatic: We take the Way of High Heaven as model and examine the present statutes; we therefore appoint four empresses to govern the six palaces within, that they may broadly assist in gentle virtue and widely maintain the sacrificial grain."

sentences.zh: 比殊禮雖降，稱謂曷宜，其因天之象，增錫嘉名。

translations.literal: Although special rites were reduced, how could the titles be fitting? Let them follow Heaven's image and be granted enhanced honorable names.
translations.idiomatic: Although special rites were reduced, how could the titles be fitting? Let them follow Heaven's image and be granted enhanced honorable names.

sentences.zh: 」於是后與三皇后並加

translations.literal: Thereupon the empress and the three empresses were all additionally given
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon the empress and the three empresses were all additionally given

translations.literal: (Grand)
translations.idiomatic: (Grand)

sentences.zh: 〔大〕焉。

translations.literal: [Great] titles.
translations.idiomatic: [Great] titles.

sentences.zh: 帝遣使持節册后為天元大皇后曰：「咨爾含章載德，體順居貞，肅恭享祀，儀刑邦國，是用嘉茲顯號，式暢徽音。

translations.literal: The emperor dispatched an envoy bearing credentials to invest the empress as Heavenly Primordial Grand Empress, stating: "You who embrace virtue and bear emblem, embody compliance and hold to rectitude, reverently perform sacrifice and serve as model to the realm—for this we grant this illustrious title and extend this fine renown.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor dispatched an envoy bearing credentials to invest the empress as Heavenly Primordial Grand Empress, stating: "You who embrace virtue and bear emblem, embody compliance and hold to rectitude, reverently perform sacrifice and serve as model to the realm—for this we grant this illustrious title and extend this fine renown.

sentences.zh: 爾其敬踐厥猷，寅荅靈命，對揚休烈，可不慎歟。

translations.literal: Reverently carry out your charge, respectfully answer the sacred mandate, and respond to this glorious enterprise—can you not be careful?"
translations.idiomatic: Reverently carry out your charge, respectfully answer the sacred mandate, and respond to this glorious enterprise—can you not be careful?"

sentences.zh: 」尋又立

translations.literal: Soon afterward she was also installed
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward she was also installed

translations.literal: (as)
translations.idiomatic: (as)

sentences.zh: 天中大皇后，與后為五皇后。

translations.literal: Heavenly Central Grand Empress, making five empresses together with her.
translations.idiomatic: Heavenly Central Grand Empress, making five empresses together with her.

sentences.zh: 后性柔婉，不妒忌，四皇后及嬪禦等咸愛而仰之。

translations.literal: The empress was gentle and compliant by nature and free of jealousy; the four empresses and the consorts and imperial ladies all loved and looked up to her.
translations.idiomatic: The empress was gentle and compliant by nature and free of jealousy; the four empresses and the consorts and imperial ladies all loved and looked up to her.

sentences.zh: 帝後昏暴滋甚，喜怒乖度。

translations.literal: Afterward the emperor grew ever more benighted and violent, and joy and anger departed from measure.
translations.idiomatic: Afterward Emperor Xuan Yuwen Yun grew ever more benighted and violent, and joy and anger departed from measure.

sentences.zh: 嘗譴后，欲加之罪，后進止詳閑，辭色不撓。

translations.literal: Once he rebuked the empress and wished to charge her with a crime; the empress in her movements was composed and detailed, and her words and expression did not waver.
translations.idiomatic: Once he rebuked the empress and wished to charge her with a crime; the empress in her movements was composed and detailed, and her words and expression did not waver.

sentences.zh: 帝大怒，遂賜后死，逼令引訣。

translations.literal: The emperor was greatly enraged and thereupon ordered the empress to die, forcing her to take farewell.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was greatly enraged and thereupon ordered the empress to die, forcing her to take farewell.

sentences.zh: 后母獨孤氏聞之，詣閤陳謝，叩頭流血，然後得免。

translations.literal: When the empress's mother, Lady Dugu, heard of it, she came to the gate to offer apology, knocking her head until blood flowed, and only then was the empress spared.
translations.idiomatic: When the empress's mother, Lady Dugu, heard of it, she came to the gate to offer apology, knocking her head until blood flowed, and only then was the empress spared.

sentences.zh: 帝崩，靜帝尊後為皇太后，居弘聖宮。

translations.literal: When the emperor died, Emperor Jing Yuwen Chan honored her as empress dowager, and she resided at Hongsheng Palace.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Xuan Yuwen Yun died, Emperor Jing Yuwen Chan honored her as empress dowager, and she resided at Hongsheng Palace.

sentences.zh: 初，宣帝不豫，詔后父入禁中侍疾。

translations.literal: Initially, when Emperor Xuan Yuwen Yun fell ill, an edict ordered the empress's father to enter the inner palace to attend him.
translations.idiomatic: Initially, when Emperor Xuan Yuwen Yun fell ill, an edict ordered the empress's father to enter the inner palace to attend him.

sentences.zh: 及大漸，劉昉、鄭譯等因矯詔以后父受遺輔政。

translations.literal: When he was near death, Liu Fang, Zheng Yi, and others used a forged edict so that the empress's father received the dying charge and assisted in government.
translations.idiomatic: When he was near death, Liu Fang, Zheng Yi, and others used a forged edict so that the empress's father received the dying charge and assisted in government.

sentences.zh: 后初雖不預謀，然以嗣主幼沖，恐權在他族，不利於己，聞昉、譯已行此詔，心甚悅之。

translations.literal: The empress at first had not taken part in the plot, but because the successor ruler was young and she feared power would fall to another clan to her own detriment, when she heard Liu Fang and Zheng Yi had already carried out this edict her heart was greatly pleased.
translations.idiomatic: The empress at first had not taken part in the plot, but because the successor ruler was young and she feared power would fall to another clan to her own detriment, when she heard Liu Fang and Zheng Yi had already carried out this edict her heart was greatly pleased.

sentences.zh: 後知其父有異圖，意頗不平，形於言色。

translations.literal: Later, when she learned her father had other designs, she was somewhat displeased and showed it in her words and expression.
translations.idiomatic: Later, when she learned her father had other designs, she was somewhat displeased and showed it in her words and expression.

sentences.zh: 及行禪代，憤惋逾甚。

translations.literal: When the abdication and dynastic change took place, her indignation and resentment grew ever greater.
translations.idiomatic: When the abdication and dynastic change took place, her indignation and resentment grew ever greater.

sentences.zh: 隋文帝旣不能譴責，內甚愧之。

translations.literal: Sui Emperor Wen Yang Jian could not bring himself to reprimand her; inwardly he felt deeply ashamed toward her.
translations.idiomatic: Sui Emperor Wen Yang Jian could not bring himself to reprimand her; inwardly he felt deeply ashamed toward her.

sentences.zh: 開皇六年，封后為樂平公主。

translations.literal: In the sixth year of Kaihuang, the empress was enfeoffed as Princess of Leping.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year of Kaihuang, the empress was enfeoffed as Princess of Leping.

sentences.zh: 后又議奪其志，后誓不許，乃止。

translations.literal: Others again proposed that she abandon her resolve; the empress vowed she would not consent, and the matter stopped.
translations.idiomatic: Others again proposed that she abandon her resolve; the empress vowed she would not consent, and the matter stopped.

sentences.zh: 大業五年，從煬帝幸張掖，殂於河西，年四十九。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Daye, accompanying Sui Emperor Yang on a visit to Zhangye, she died in Hexi, aged forty-nine.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year of Daye, accompanying Sui Emperor Yang on a visit to Zhangye, she died in Hexi, aged forty-nine.

sentences.zh: 煬帝還京，詔有司備禮，祔葬后於定陵。

translations.literal: When Sui Emperor Yang returned to the capital, an edict ordered the responsible offices to prepare rites and had her buried by joint interment at Dingling.
translations.idiomatic: When Sui Emperor Yang returned to the capital, an edict ordered the responsible offices to prepare rites and had her buried by joint interment at Dingling.

sentences.zh: 宣帝朱皇后名滿月，吳人也。

translations.literal: Empress Zhu, consort of Emperor Xuan Yuwen Yun, was named Manyue; she was a native of Wu.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Zhu, consort of Emperor Xuan Yuwen Yun, was named Manyue; she was a native of Wu.

sentences.zh: 其家坐事，沒入東宮。

translations.literal: Her family was implicated in a crime and confiscated into the Eastern Palace.
translations.idiomatic: Her family was implicated in a crime and confiscated into the Eastern Palace.

sentences.zh: 帝之為太子，后被選掌帝衣服。

translations.literal: While Emperor Xuan Yuwen Yun was crown prince, she was selected to manage his clothing.
translations.idiomatic: While Emperor Xuan Yuwen Yun was crown prince, she was selected to manage his clothing.

sentences.zh: 帝年少，召而幸之，遂生靜帝。

translations.literal: The emperor was young; he summoned and favored her, and she bore Emperor Jing Yuwen Chan.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was young; he summoned and favored her, and she bore Emperor Jing Yuwen Chan.

sentences.zh: 大象元年，立為天元帝后，尋改為天皇后。

translations.literal: First year of Daxiang, she was installed as empress of the Heavenly Primordial Emperor; soon after she was retitled Heavenly Empress.
translations.idiomatic: First year of Daxiang, she was installed as empress of the Heavenly Primordial Emperor; soon after she was retitled Heavenly Empress.

sentences.zh: 二年，又改為天大皇后。

translations.literal: Second year, she was again retitled Grand Heavenly Empress.
translations.idiomatic: Second year, she was again retitled Grand Heavenly Empress.

sentences.zh: 册曰：「咨爾彌宣四德，訓范六宮，軒庭列序，堯門表慶，嘉稱旣降，盛典宜膺。

translations.literal: The edict of investiture stated: "I address you thus: You have fully displayed the four virtues and set the pattern for the six palaces; the court ranks in proper order, and the Gate of Yao proclaims celebration. Worthy acclaim has descended; the grand ceremony is fittingly yours to receive.
translations.idiomatic: The edict of investiture stated: "I address you thus: You have fully displayed the four virtues and set the pattern for the six palaces; the court ranks in proper order, and the Gate of Yao proclaims celebration. Worthy acclaim has descended; the grand ceremony is fittingly yours to receive.

sentences.zh: 爾其飾性履道，無愆禮正，永固休祉，可不慎歟。

translations.literal: Adorn your nature and walk the Way, without fault in ritual propriety; may blessed fortune endure forever—can you not be careful?"
translations.idiomatic: Adorn your nature and walk the Way, without fault in ritual propriety; may blessed fortune endure forever—can you not be careful?"

sentences.zh: 」后本非良家子，又年長於帝十餘歲，疎賤無寵。

translations.literal: " The empress was not originally from a good family; she was also more than ten years older than the emperor, distant and lowly, without favor.
translations.idiomatic: The empress was not originally from a good family; she was also more than ten years older than the emperor, distant and lowly, and without favor.

sentences.zh: 以靜帝故，特尊崇之，班亞楊皇后焉。

translations.literal: Because of Emperor Jing Yuwen Chan, she was specially honored and ranked just below Empress Yang.
translations.idiomatic: Because of Emperor Jing Yuwen Chan, she was specially honored and ranked just below Empress Yang.

sentences.zh: 宣帝崩，靜帝尊為帝太

translations.literal: When Emperor Xuan Yuwen Yun died, Emperor Jing Yuwen Chan honored her as Imperial
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Xuan Yuwen Yun died, Emperor Jing Yuwen Chan honored her as Imperial

translations.literal: (Empress)
translations.idiomatic: (Empress)

sentences.zh: 后。

translations.literal: Dowager.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Dowager.

sentences.zh: 隋開皇元年，出俗為尼，名法淨。

translations.literal: In the first year of Kaihuang of Sui, she left the lay life to become a nun, taking the name Fajing.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Kaihuang of Sui, she left the lay life to become a nun, taking the name Fajing.

sentences.zh: 六年殂，年四十，以尼禮葬京城。

translations.literal: In the sixth year she died, aged forty; she was buried in the capital by rites for nuns.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year she died, aged forty; she was buried in the capital by rites for nuns.

sentences.zh: 宣帝陳皇后名月儀，自云潁川人，大將軍山提第八女也。

translations.literal: Empress Chen, consort of Emperor Xuan Yuwen Yun, was named Yueyi; she claimed to be from Yingchuan, the eighth daughter of Grand General Shanti.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Chen, consort of Emperor Xuan Yuwen Yun, was named Yueyi; she claimed to be from Yingchuan, the eighth daughter of Grand General Shanti.

sentences.zh: 大象元年六月，以選入宮，拜為德妃。

translations.literal: Sixth month of the first year of Daxiang, selected to enter the palace, she was appointed Virtuous Consort.
translations.idiomatic: Sixth month of the first year of Daxiang, selected to enter the palace, she was appointed Virtuous Consort.

sentences.zh: 月餘，立為天左皇后。

translations.literal: After a month and more, she was installed as Heavenly Left Empress.
translations.idiomatic: After a month and more, she was installed as Heavenly Left Empress.

sentences.zh: 二年二月，改天左大皇后。

translations.literal: Second month of the second year, she was retitled Grand Heavenly Left Empress.
translations.idiomatic: Second month of the second year, she was retitled Grand Heavenly Left Empress.

sentences.zh: 册曰：「咨爾儀範柔閑，操履凝潔，淑問彰於遠近，令則冠於宮闈。

translations.literal: The edict of investiture stated: "I address you thus: Your bearing is gentle and serene, your conduct pure and unstained; your fine reputation shines near and far, and your exemplary rule crowns the inner palace.
translations.idiomatic: The edict of investiture stated: "I address you thus: Your bearing is gentle and serene, your conduct pure and unstained; your fine reputation shines near and far, and your exemplary rule crowns the inner palace.

sentences.zh: 是用申彼寵章，加茲徽號。

translations.literal: Therefore I extend this favor and bestow this honored title.
translations.idiomatic: Therefore I extend this favor and bestow this honored title.

sentences.zh: 爾其復禮問詩，披圖顧史，永隆嘉命，可不慎歟。

translations.literal: Return to rites and to the Book of Odes, unfold the charts and consult the histories; may this honored mandate flourish forever—can you not be careful?"
translations.idiomatic: Return to rites and to the Book of Odes, unfold the charts and consult the histories; may this honored mandate flourish forever—can you not be careful?"

sentences.zh: 」三月，又詔曰：「正內之重，風化之基，嘉耦之制，代多殊典。

translations.literal: " Third month, another edict stated: "The weight of the inner court is the foundation of transformation by custom; the institution of worthy marriage differs in each age with many distinct precedents.
translations.idiomatic: Third month, another edict stated: "The weight of the inner court is the foundation of transformation by custom; the institution of worthy marriage differs in each age with many distinct precedents.

sentences.zh: 軒、嚳繼軌，次妃並四；

translations.literal: Xuan and Ku continued the precedent, and secondary consorts numbered four together;
translations.idiomatic: Xuan and Ku continued the precedent, and secondary consorts numbered four together;

sentences.zh: 虞舜受命，厥娶猶三。

translations.literal: when Shun of Yu received the mandate, his marriages still numbered three.
translations.idiomatic: when Shun of Yu received the mandate, his marriages still numbered three.

sentences.zh: 禮非相襲，隨時不無。

translations.literal: Rites are not simply inherited; in keeping with the times there is always change.
translations.idiomatic: Rites are not simply inherited; in keeping with the times there is always change.

sentences.zh: 朕祗承寶圖，載弘徽號，自我改作，超革先古。

translations.literal: We reverently receive the sacred chart, bearing forth grand titles; from now we remake them, surpassing and reforming antiquity.
translations.idiomatic: We reverently receive the sacred chart, bearing forth grand titles; from now we remake them, surpassing and reforming antiquity.

sentences.zh: 曰天元居極，五帝所以仰崇；

translations.literal: Thus the Heavenly Primordial occupies the apex, and the Five Emperors were therefore revered on high;
translations.idiomatic: Thus the Heavenly Primordial occupies the apex, and the Five Emperors were therefore revered on high;

sentences.zh: 王者稱尊，列後於焉上儷。

translations.literal: when the king is called exalted, the ranked consorts stand paired with him above.
translations.idiomatic: when the king is called exalted, the ranked consorts stand paired with him above.

sentences.zh: 且坤儀比德，土數惟五，旣縟恒典，宜取斯儀。

translations.literal: Moreover the queenly figure matches virtue, and the earth's number is five; since the constant rites are already elaborate, this measure should be taken.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover the queenly figure matches virtue, and the earth's number is five; since the constant rites are already elaborate, this measure should be taken.

sentences.zh: 四大皇后外，可增置天中大皇后一人。

translations.literal: Beyond the four great empresses, one Heavenly Central Grand Empress may additionally be established.
translations.idiomatic: Beyond the four great empresses, one Heavenly Central Grand Empress may additionally be established.

sentences.zh: 天中大皇后爰主粢盛，徽音日躋，肇建嘉名，宜膺顯册。

translations.literal: The Heavenly Central Grand Empress shall preside over the sacrificial grain; her fine renown daily ascends; this auspicious title is newly established and fittingly receives the manifest proclamation.
translations.idiomatic: The Heavenly Central Grand Empress shall preside over the sacrificial grain; her fine renown daily ascends; this auspicious title is newly established and fittingly receives the manifest proclamation.

sentences.zh: 」於是以后為天中大皇后。

translations.literal: " Thereupon the empress was made Heavenly Central Grand Empress.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon the empress was made Heavenly Central Grand Empress.

sentences.zh: 帝崩，后出家為尼，改名華光。

translations.literal: When the emperor died, the empress left home to become a nun, changing her name to Huaguang.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Xuan Yuwen Yun died, the empress left home to become a nun, changing her name to Huaguang.

sentences.zh: 宣帝尉遲皇后名熾繁，蜀國公迥之孫女。

translations.literal: Empress Yuchi, consort of Emperor Xuan Yuwen Yun, was named Chifan, granddaughter of Duke of Shu Yuchi Jiong.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Yuchi, consort of Emperor Xuan Yuwen Yun, was named Chifan, granddaughter of Duke of Shu Yuchi Jiong.

sentences.zh: 有美色。

translations.literal: She had beautiful features.
translations.idiomatic: She had beautiful features.

sentences.zh: 初適杞國公亮子西陽公溫，以宗婦例入朝，帝逼而幸之。

translations.literal: Initially she married Wen, Duke of Xiyang, son of Liang, Duke of Qi State; entering court by the precedent for consorts of the imperial clan, the emperor forced and favored her.
translations.idiomatic: Initially she married Wen, Duke of Xiyang, son of Liang, Duke of Qi State; entering court by the precedent for consorts of the imperial clan, Emperor Xuan Yuwen Yun forced and favored her.

sentences.zh: 及亮謀逆，帝誅溫，進後入宮，拜為長貴妃。

translations.literal: When Liang plotted rebellion, the emperor executed Wen and had her enter the palace, appointing her Senior Noble Consort.
translations.idiomatic: When Liang plotted rebellion, the emperor executed Wen and had her enter the palace, appointing her Senior Noble Consort.

sentences.zh: 大象二年三月，立為天左大皇后。

translations.literal: Third month of the second year of Daxiang, she was installed as Grand Heavenly Left Empress.
translations.idiomatic: Third month of the second year of Daxiang, she was installed as Grand Heavenly Left Empress.

sentences.zh: 册曰：「咨爾門膺積善，躬表靈貺，徽音茂德，朕實嘉之。

translations.literal: The edict of investiture stated: "I address you thus: Your house has received accumulated merit; your person displays heaven's favor; your fine renown and abundant virtue—I truly commend them.
translations.idiomatic: The edict of investiture stated: "I address you thus: Your house has received accumulated merit; your person displays heaven's favor; your fine renown and abundant virtue—I truly commend them.

sentences.zh: 是用弘茲盛典，申彼寵章。

translations.literal: Therefore I extend this grand ceremony and convey this favor.
translations.idiomatic: Therefore I extend this grand ceremony and convey this favor.

sentences.zh: 爾其克慎厥猷，寅荅景命，永承休烈，可不慎歟。

translations.literal: Diligently heed your course, reverently answer heaven's mandate, and forever inherit glorious fortune—can you not be careful?"
translations.idiomatic: Diligently heed your course, reverently answer heaven's mandate, and forever inherit glorious fortune—can you not be careful?"

sentences.zh: 」帝崩，后出俗為尼，改名華首。

translations.literal: " When the emperor died, the empress left the lay life to become a nun, changing her name to Huashou.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Xuan Yuwen Yun died, the empress left the lay life to become a nun, changing her name to Huashou.

sentences.zh: 隋開皇十五年，殂，年三十。

translations.literal: In the fifteenth year of Kaihuang of Sui, she died, aged thirty.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifteenth year of Kaihuang of Sui, she died, aged thirty.

sentences.zh: 史臣曰：孔子稱「夷狄之有君，不如諸夏之亡也」。

translations.literal: The historian writes: Confucius said, "The barbarians may have their rulers, but they cannot compare with the Central States when they lack them."
translations.idiomatic: The historian writes: Confucius said, "The barbarians may have their rulers, but they cannot compare with the Central States when they lack them."

sentences.zh: 是以周納狄后，富辰謂之禍階；

translations.literal: Hence when Zhou accepted the Di empress, Fuchen called it the steps to disaster;
translations.idiomatic: Hence when Zhou accepted the Di empress, Fuchen called it the steps to disaster;

sentences.zh: 晉升戎女，卜人以為不吉。

translations.literal: when Jin elevated a Rong woman, the diviners considered it inauspicious.
translations.idiomatic: when Jin elevated a Rong woman, the diviners considered it inauspicious.

sentences.zh: 斯固非謬焉。

translations.literal: This was certainly not mistaken.
translations.idiomatic: This was certainly not mistaken.

sentences.zh: 自周氏受命，逮乎高祖，年踰三紀，世歷四君。

translations.literal: From when the Zhou house received the mandate until High Ancestor Yuwen Yong, more than three decades passed and four rulers succeeded one another.
translations.idiomatic: From when the Zhou house received the mandate until High Ancestor Yuwen Yong, more than three decades passed and four rulers succeeded one another.

sentences.zh: 業非草昧之辰，事殊權宜之日，乃弃同卽異，以夷亂華。

translations.literal: The enterprise was no longer in its founding period; affairs differed from days of expedient measure—yet they abandoned the same for the different and used barbarians to disorder the Chinese.
translations.idiomatic: The enterprise was no longer in its founding period; affairs differed from days of expedient measure—yet they abandoned kin for outsiders and used barbarians to disorder the Chinese.

sentences.zh: 捐婚姻之彝序，求豺狼之外利。

translations.literal: They cast aside the canonical order of marriage and sought external profit from wolves.
translations.idiomatic: They cast aside the canonical order of marriage and sought external profit from wolves.

sentences.zh: 旣而報者倦矣，施者無厭，向之所謂和親，未幾已成讐敵。

translations.literal: Before long those who repaid grew weary and those who bestowed were insatiable; what had been called harmony-through-kinship before, in no time had become sworn enemies.
translations.idiomatic: Before long those who repaid grew weary and those who bestowed were insatiable; what had been called harmony-through-kinship before, in no time had become sworn enemies.

sentences.zh: 奇正之道，有異於斯。

translations.literal: The way of the orthodox and the unorthodox differs from this.
translations.idiomatic: The way of the orthodox and the unorthodox differs from this.

sentences.zh: 于時高祖雖受制於人，未親庶政，而謀士韞奇，直臣鉗口。

translations.literal: At that time, although High Ancestor Yuwen Yong was controlled by others and did not personally attend to general government, yet strategists hoarded their plans and upright ministers were silenced.
translations.idiomatic: At that time, although High Ancestor Yuwen Yong was controlled by others and did not personally attend to general government, yet strategists hoarded their plans and upright ministers were silenced.

sentences.zh: 過矣哉！

translations.literal: An error indeed!
translations.idiomatic: An error indeed!

sentences.zh: 歷觀前載，以外戚而居宰輔者多矣。

translations.literal: Reviewing former records, many have occupied the chief minister's post as maternal kin.
translations.idiomatic: Reviewing former records, many have occupied the chief minister's post as maternal kin.

sentences.zh: 申、呂則曠代無聞，呂、霍則與時俱盛。

translations.literal: Shen and Lü went unmentioned for ages; Lü and Huo flourished together with their times.
translations.idiomatic: Shen and Lü went unmentioned for ages; Lü and Huo flourished together with their times.

sentences.zh: 傾漢室者王族，喪周祚者楊氏。

translations.literal: The Wang clan overturned the Han house; the Yang clan ended Zhou's fortune.
translations.idiomatic: The Wang clan overturned the Han house; the Yang clan ended Zhou's fortune.

sentences.zh: 何滅亡之禍，合若符契焉。

translations.literal: How the calamity of extinction matched like tally and seal!
translations.idiomatic: How the calamity of extinction matched like tally and seal!
